title: One more favour
setting: Late on a school night at Yuki's flat. Her little brother Kenji turns up at the door without warning, looking glum. Later their mother comes on the phone.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, kenji? nande koko ni iru no? mou konna jikan da yo.
lines.ja: え、ケンジ？なんでここにいるの？もうこんな時間だよ。
lines.kana: え、けんじ？なんでここにいるの？もうこんなじかんだよ。
lines.english: Kenji? What are you doing here? It's so late!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: neechan, gomen. chotto onegai ga aru n da kedo.
lines.ja: 姉ちゃん、ごめん。ちょっとお願いがあるんだけど。
lines.kana: ねえちゃん、ごめん。ちょっとおねがいがあるんだけど。
lines.english: Sorry, sis. There's something I need to ask you.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: dou shita no? nanka genki nai jan.
lines.ja: どうしたの？なんか元気ないじゃん。
lines.kana: どうしたの？なんかげんきないじゃん。
lines.english: What's wrong? You seem kind of down.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shiken, zenbu dame datta. uchi ni kaeritakunakute.
lines.ja: 試験、全部ダメだった。うちに帰りたくなくて。
lines.kana: しけん、ぜんぶだめだった。うちにかえりたくなくて。
lines.english: My exams all went badly. I didn't want to go home.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.kana: そっか。で、おねがいって？
lines.english: I see. So what's the favour?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: neechan ni meiwaku kakeru no wa wakatteru kedo, konban, tomete kurenai?
lines.ja: 姉ちゃんに迷惑かけるのはわかってるけど、今晩、泊めてくれない？
lines.kana: ねえちゃんにめいわくかけるのはわかってるけど、こんばん、とめてくれない？
lines.english: I know I'm putting you out, but can I stay at yours tonight?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii kedo, okaasan ni wa renraku shita no?
lines.ja: いいけど、お母さんには連絡したの？
lines.kana: いいけど、おかあさんにはれんらくしたの？
lines.english: Sure, but did you tell Mom?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: してない。スマホ、うちに忘れちゃった。
lines.kana: してない。すまほ、うちにわすれちゃった。
lines.english: No. I left my phone at home.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e! okaasan, zettai shinpai shiteru yo.
lines.ja: え！お母さん、絶対心配してるよ。
lines.kana: え！おかあさん、ぜったいしんぱいしてるよ。
lines.english: What? Mom must be worried sick!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: dakara, mou hitotsu onegai ga aru n da. neechan kara denwa kakete kurenai?
lines.ja: だから、もう一つお願いがあるんだ。姉ちゃんから電話かけてくれない？
lines.kana: だから、もうひとつおねがいがあるんだ。ねえちゃんからでんわかけてくれない？
lines.english: That's why I've got one more favour. Could you call her for me?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: wakatta. moshimoshi, okaasan? kenji, ima watashi no tokoro ni iru yo.
lines.ja: わかった。もしもし、お母さん？ケンジ、今私のところにいるよ。
lines.kana: わかった。もしもし、おかあさん？けんじ、いまわたしのところにいるよ。
lines.english: Okay. Hello, Mom? Kenji's here at my place.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: aa, yokatta. renraku mo nai kara, honto ni shinpai shita no yo.
lines.ja: ああ、よかった。連絡もないから、ほんとに心配したのよ。
lines.kana: ああ、よかった。れんらくもないから、ほんとにしんぱいしたのよ。
lines.english: Oh, thank goodness. Not a word from him, I was so worried.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, okaasan? shinpai kakete gomen. shiken, dame datta n da.
lines.ja: もしもし、お母さん？心配かけてごめん。試験、ダメだったんだ。
lines.kana: もしもし、おかあさん？しんぱいかけてごめん。しけん、だめだったんだ。
lines.english: Hello, Mom? Sorry I worried you. My exams went badly.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shiken no koto wa ii no. tsugi ganbareba ii n da kara, genki dashite.
lines.ja: 試験のことはいいの。次がんばればいいんだから、元気出して。
lines.kana: しけんのことはいいの。つぎがんばればいいんだから、げんきだして。
lines.english: Forget about the exams. You can just try harder next time, so cheer up.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: 姉ちゃん、迷惑かけてごめんね。
lines.kana: ねえちゃん、めいわくかけてごめんね。
lines.english: Sis, sorry for all the trouble.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii yo. demo, mou okaasan ni shinpai kakecha dame da yo.
lines.ja: いいよ。でも、もうお母さんに心配かけちゃダメだよ。
lines.kana: いいよ。でも、もうおかあさんにしんぱいかけちゃだめだよ。
lines.english: It's fine. But don't make Mom worry like that again.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ato hitotsu dake, onegai ga aru n da kedo. ashita, issho ni uchi ni kaette kurenai?
lines.ja: あと一つだけ、お願いがあるんだけど。明日、一緒にうちに帰ってくれない？
lines.kana: あとひとつだけ、おねがいがあるんだけど。あした、いっしょにうちにかえってくれない？
lines.english: There's just one more thing I need to ask. Will you come home with me tomorrow?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mada aru no? hai hai, sono onegai mo kiite ageru kara, genki dashite.
lines.ja: まだあるの？はいはい、そのお願いも聞いてあげるから、元気出して。
lines.kana: まだあるの？はいはい、そのおねがいもきいてあげるから、げんきだして。
lines.english: There's more? Okay, okay, I'll do that one too, so cheer up.

choices.english: Kenji missed the last train, so Yuki lets him stay and keeps it from their mother.
Their mother is angry about Kenji's exams, so Yuki phones her to calm her down.
Kenji turns up after bad exams, and Yuki phones their mother, who was only worried.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Kenji's exams went badly and he didn't want to go home, so in line 6 he asks to stay the night. He left his phone at home (line 8), so in line 10 he asks Yuki to call their mother. Mom is relieved (line 12: aa, yokatta) and tells him to forget about the exams (line 14: shiken no koto wa ii no). A is wrong: nobody mentions the last train. Kenji came because he didn't want to go home, and Yuki phones their mother instead of keeping it from her. B is wrong: Yuki does phone her, but Mom isn't angry. She was worried (line 12) and says never mind the exams (line 14).

questions.english: Near the end, Kenji says, "ato hitotsu dake, onegai ga aru n da kedo." What happens?
questions.ja: 最後に、何がありましたか？
questions.kana: さいごに、なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: saigo ni, nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji asks Yuki to go home with him tomorrow, and she says yes.
Kenji offers to do Yuki a favour tomorrow, to make up for tonight.
Kenji asks Yuki to call their mother again, but she says no.

questions.explanation: Line 17: onegai ga aru opens a request, so Kenji is the one asking: ashita, issho ni uchi ni kaette kurenai? (will you come home with me tomorrow?). In line 18 Yuki says sono onegai mo kiite ageru. onegai o kiku is the other side of it, granting a favour. This is the third time Kenji says onegai ga aru (line 2 led to staying the night, line 10 to phoning Mom), which is why Yuki says mada aru no? (there's more?). B gets the direction backwards: onegai ga aru doesn't mean offering to do someone a favour, and Kenji offers nothing. C is wrong: Yuki already phoned their mother in line 11, and in the end she agrees instead of refusing.

questions.english: After the phone call, how does Kenji apologise to Yuki?
questions.ja: 電話のあと、ケンジはユキに何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: でんわのあと、けんじはゆきになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: denwa no ato, kenji wa yuki ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Sis, sorry for causing trouble (okosu, like English 'cause').
Sis, sorry for all the trouble.
Sis, sorry for being bothered (meiwaku suru).

questions.explanation: Line 15: 'neechan, meiwaku kakete gomen ne.' Trouble you cause someone is put on them with kakeru. Kenji also uses it in line 6 (meiwaku kakeru no wa wakatteru kedo: I know I'm putting you out). A is a calque of English 'cause trouble': okosu works for incidents (mondai o okosu), but meiwaku doesn't take it. C uses meiwaku suru, which describes the person being bothered, so it turns the apology around.

questions.english: Imagine you're Kenji, back home the next day. Okaasan says to you, "kenji, kinou wa honto ni shinpai shita no yo." Apologise for worrying her, using shinpai o kakeru.
questions.ja: ケンジ、昨日はほんとに心配したのよ。
questions.kana: けんじ、きのうはほんとにしんぱいしたのよ。
questions.romaji: kenji, kinou wa honto ni shinpai shita no yo.
questions.answer: Say sorry for making her worry: shinpai kakete gomen (the o drops in casual speech). She was the one who worried (shinpai shita), and you put the worry on her with kakeru.

modelAnswers.romaji: shinpai kakete gomen. kondo kara chanto renraku suru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 心配かけてごめん。今度からちゃんと連絡するよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry I worried you. From now on I'll let you know.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen ne, shinpai kakechatte. sumaho, uchi ni wasurechatta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんね、心配かけちゃって。スマホ、うちに忘れちゃったんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry for making you worry. I'd left my phone at home.

questions.explanation: Kenji says this to Mom on the phone (line 13: shinpai kakete gomen), and Yuki warns him in line 16 (mou okaasan ni shinpai kakecha dame da yo). Notice who does what. Mom says shinpai shita (line 12) and Yuki says okaasan, zettai shinpai shiteru yo (line 9), because Mom is the one worrying. When you're the cause, you put the worry on her with kakeru. 'shinpai shite gomen' would mean you were the one worrying, which makes no sense here. She's your mother, so casual speech fits. With someone like Tanaka-san you'd say shinpai o kakete sumimasen.

questions.english: Imagine you're Yuki. A week later, Kenji mumbles, "neechan, mata shiken dame datta." He's clearly down. Cheer him up using genki o dasu.
questions.ja: 姉ちゃん、また試験ダメだった。
questions.kana: ねえちゃん、またしけんだめだった。
questions.answer: Tell him to cheer up: genki dashite (the o drops in casual speech). You can soften it with daijoubu da yo, or add that there's always next time. Don't lead with ganbatte, which tells him to keep trying when what he needs is to feel better.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu da yo, genki dashite. tsugi ga aru jan.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫だよ、元気出して。次があるじゃん。
modelAnswers.english: It's okay, cheer up. There's always next time.

modelAnswers.romaji: sokka. maa, genki dashite. nanka oishii mono demo tabe ni iku?
modelAnswers.ja: そっか。まあ、元気出して。なんかおいしいものでも食べに行く？
modelAnswers.english: I see. Well, cheer up. Want to go get something nice to eat?

questions.explanation: Mom (line 14) and Yuki (line 18) both say genki dashite to Kenji while he's down. Line 14 also lets you hear the contrast. tsugi ganbareba ii (you can just try harder next time) is about effort later, while genki dashite is about feeling better now. ganbatte on its own can feel like pressure to someone who's already low, and genki ni natte is what you say to someone who's ill (get well). Kenji is family, so casual speech fits.

newWords.english: big sis (what a younger sibling calls an older sister)
let someone stay the night (tomete kurenai?: can I stay at yours?)
try hard, hang in there (ganbareba: if you try hard)
